contexts.statement: Source-grounded review of all thirteen old Argus family 028 artifacts listed in PRIOR_DRAFTS.json under OBJECTIVE.md; no new manuscript-error search or whole-paper certification.

definitions.review_universe: 13 artifacts; 23 old claims; 23 graph nodes; 16 routes; 16 judgement records; one developed argument and fourteen reference-only dependencies
definitions.source_version: OpenAI, Bounded-Step Walks on Gaussian Primes, September 26, 2026; supplied manuscript manifest revision 4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae
definitions.rectangle: Fixed before sampling; centered at zero; arbitrary real orientation; R>=W>=1; independent fair conjugates of supplied norm-p factors over distinct primes p=1 mod 4 in [T,2T], T>=5; P=product p; 0<d<1/4; RW<=P^(1-d)
definitions.acceptance: Engineer prose judgements and scoped computation only; no Lean/kernel evidence, no global priority claim, native independent Reviewer required

claims.natural_statement: For every r>=1, T>=5, distinct rational primes p_i=1 mod 4 in [T,2T], supplied norm-p_i Gaussian factors alpha_i, 0<d<1/4, and every fixed-before-signs centered rectangle of arbitrary orientation with R>=W>=1 and RW<=P^(1-d), independent fair choices pi_i in {alpha_i,conj(alpha_i)} satisfy Pr(Q intersect (product pi_i) Z[i] != {0}) <= min(1,3 exp(-d^2 r/32)). This is the old proposed bound, not a new improvement made by this review.

external_assumptions.statement: Every ordinary prime p congruent to 1 modulo 4 has norm-p Gaussian prime factors that are conjugate and nonassociate. The rectangle theorem explicitly takes such factors as input.
external_assumptions.source: Keith Conrad, The Gaussian Integers, local archived PDF SHA-256 0a9d42f7eecfc8e57f28277a153042f8e05b4d295982856864b8bbd8fabb3479, Theorem 9.7(ii); inspected text lines 1378-1389 and PDF/text equality checked. Mutable notes, no canonical version identifier asserted.

external_assumptions.statement: Ordinary real exponential power-series calculus, Markov inequality and finite conditional-expectation/tower rules are trusted background; no general concentration theorem is assumed.
external_assumptions.source: Background rules used explicitly in old signed_rectangle/PROOF.md sections 2, 3 and 5, SHA-256 ea40e38714121560a32f1e5509ed326fc28d553dcc89b66f560416d5b4268e80; exact use read in research/draft_reviews/signed_rectangle/report.md. The fair-bit and cube concentration inequalities themselves are rederived there.

claims.natural_statement: Under the rectangle context and d^2 r>=1, every fixed primitive integer line has nonzero witness probability at most exp(-d^2 r/8), uniformly in the direction; this bound alone does not count possible witness lines.

claims.natural_statement: The old rectangle proof and local exact checker do not certify the other fourteen manuscript-only dependency claims, the finite sieve obstruction or the full Gaussian-prime component theorem. The retired fixed-line union route and outcome-dependent rectangle construction are not refutations of the actual fixed-rectangle manuscript lemma.

routes.retired_because: Historical R_FIXED_LINE_UNION_ONLY is insufficient: a per-line tail supplies no parameter-uniform bound on the number of primitive witness lines to sum. The developed proof instead uses separated classes and a two-union concentration argument. This retires a proof route, not a manuscript assertion.
